+# Feature Specification: Room Handling During Cross-Space Moves
+
+**Feature Branch**: `084-move-room-handling`
+**Created**: 2026-03-30
+**Status**: Draft
+**Scope**: Backend (server) — communication layer integration
+**Input**: Clarification of Matrix/Synapse room handling for cross-space move operations
+**Related**: `083-cross-space-moves` (parent feature), `080-move-spaces` (broader vision)
+
+## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
+
+### User Story 1 — Preserve Discussion Comments After Move (Priority: P1)
+
+As a user who has participated in discussions within a subspace, I want my comments and everyone else's comments to remain readable after the subspace is moved to a different space so that the collaborative history and knowledge are not lost.
+
+When a subspace (L1) is moved across L0 boundaries, every callout's discussion room retains its full comment history. Comments remain attributed to the original author. Users who navigate to the moved subspace can read the entire discussion thread exactly as it existed before the move — same messages, same authors, same order.
+
+**Why this priority**: Comments represent the accumulated knowledge and decision history of a collaborative effort. Losing them during a reorganization operation would undermine trust in the platform. This is the primary user-facing concern for communication during moves.
+
+**Independent Test**: Create an L1 subspace with a callout that has 10+ comments from different users. Move the L1 to a different L0 space. Navigate to the callout in its new location and verify all 10+ comments are visible, correctly attributed to their original authors, and in the original order.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a callout in an L1 subspace has 15 comments from 5 different users, **When** the subspace is moved to a different L0, **Then** all 15 comments are visible in the callout's discussion at the new location, each attributed to the correct original author.
+2. **Given** a callout has threaded replies and reactions on comments, **When** the subspace is moved, **Then** thread structure and reactions are preserved.
+3. **Given** an L1 subspace has multiple callouts each with their own discussion rooms, **When** the subspace is moved, **Then** every callout's comments are preserved independently.
+4. **Given** the L1 subspace has L2 sub-subspaces with their own callouts and comments, **When** the entire subtree is moved, **Then** comments in L2 callouts are also fully preserved.
+5. **Given** a subspace has been moved and a new user joins the moved space's community, **When** they navigate to a callout discussion, **Then** they can read all comments written before the move (with correct author attribution) and post new comments.
+6. **Given** a subspace has been moved and a new user joins, **When** they post a new comment to a preserved discussion room, **Then** the comment appears alongside the pre-move comments in the same thread — the discussion continues seamlessly.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 2 — Revoke Room Memberships After Move (Priority: P1)
+
+As a platform administrator, I want communication room memberships to be revoked when a subspace is moved so that former community members no longer have access to post or receive updates in rooms that belong to the moved space.
+
+When a cross-L0 move clears community memberships (as specified in `083-cross-space-moves`), the corresponding communication room memberships must also be revoked. This ensures that users who are no longer part of the community cannot continue to post messages or receive notifications from rooms in the moved space.
+
+**Why this priority**: This is co-P1 with comment preservation because it is a security and access control requirement. Without membership revocation, former community members could continue interacting with rooms they should no longer access.
+
+**Independent Test**: Create an L1 subspace with community members who have posted comments. Move the L1 to a different L0. Verify that the former members can no longer post new messages to the callout discussion rooms or the community updates room, and no longer receive notifications from those rooms.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** 10 users are members of a callout discussion room in the L1 subspace, **When** the subspace is moved to a different L0, **Then** all 10 users are removed from the room's membership. They can no longer post new messages.
+2. **Given** a user was a member of the community updates room, **When** the subspace is moved, **Then** the user no longer receives updates from that room.
+3. **Given** a user who was removed from the room navigates to the moved callout, **When** they attempt to post a comment, **Then** they receive an authorization error.
+4. **Given** a user is a member of rooms in both the moved L1 and one of its L2 sub-subspaces, **When** the subtree is moved, **Then** the user is removed from rooms at both levels.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 3 — Recreate Community Updates Room (Priority: P2)
+
+As a platform administrator, I want the community updates room to be recreated fresh after a cross-L0 move so that the new community context starts with a clean announcement channel.
+
+The community "updates" room — used for announcements and broadcasts — is recreated empty after the move. Unlike callout discussion rooms (which hold collaborative knowledge), the updates room is an administrative broadcast channel. Its history is specific to the old community context and is not meaningful in the new one.
+
+**Why this priority**: This is lower priority because the updates room is an admin broadcast channel, not a knowledge repository. Recreating it is a clean-slate approach that avoids confusion from old announcements appearing in a new community context.
+
+**Independent Test**: Create an L1 subspace, post several community updates. Move the subspace to a different L0. Verify the updates room is empty (no old announcements) and new updates can be posted by the new parent's admins.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** the L1 subspace's community updates room has 5 announcements, **When** the subspace is moved to a different L0, **Then** the updates room is recreated empty — the old announcements are not visible.
+2. **Given** the updates room has been recreated, **When** an admin of the target L0 posts an update, **Then** it appears in the new updates room successfully.
+3. **Given** the L1 has L2 sub-subspaces with their own community updates rooms, **When** the subtree is moved, **Then** each sub-subspace's updates room is also recreated empty.
+
+---
+
+### Edge Cases
+
+- **Room with no messages**: A callout discussion room that was never used (zero messages). The room should be preserved as-is — no special handling needed.
+- **Post contribution comment rooms**: Posts within callouts also have their own comment rooms. These must follow the same preservation rules as callout discussion rooms — comments preserved, memberships revoked.
+- **Membership revocation failure**: If the external messaging service is unavailable during the move, revocation failures are logged and swallowed (fire-and-forget). The move itself (database transaction) is not blocked by a messaging service outage.
+- **User who is member of both source and target communities**: A user who belongs to both the old and new L0 communities. After the move, their membership in the moved space's rooms is revoked (along with everyone else's). They would need to be re-added through the new community context if applicable.
+- **Large room membership lists**: A subspace with hundreds of room members. The membership revocation must handle batch operations efficiently without timing out.
+- **Comment author attribution after move**: Comment authorship is inherent in the messaging system — the original author's identity is stored with each message. No re-attribution or migration is needed.
+- **Concurrent message posting during move**: If a user posts a message to a room while the move is in progress, the message may succeed (if membership hasn't been revoked yet) or fail (if it has). This is acceptable — the move operation takes precedence.
+
+## Requirements *(mandatory)*
+
+### Functional Requirements
+
+#### Comment and Discussion Preservation
+
+- **FR-001**: When a space is moved across L0 boundaries, system MUST preserve all callout discussion rooms and their complete message history (comments, threads, reactions).
+- **FR-002**: Comment authorship (the association between each message and the user who wrote it) MUST remain intact after the move. No re-attribution or migration of message content is required.
+- **FR-003**: Post contribution comment rooms MUST follow the same preservation rules — comments preserved, memberships revoked.
+- **FR-004**: The local room metadata records (room entity linked to each callout and post) MUST remain intact. No room entity re-creation is needed for discussion rooms.
+- **FR-005**: The message count tracked locally for each preserved room MUST remain accurate after the move.
+
+#### Membership Revocation
+
+- **FR-006**: When community memberships are cleared during a cross-L0 move, system MUST revoke all user memberships from every communication room in the moved space and its subtree. This includes callout discussion rooms, post comment rooms, and the community updates room.
+- **FR-007**: Membership revocation MUST be performed as a batch operation across all rooms in the moved subtree.
+- **FR-008**: Membership revocation from the messaging service is a non-transactional side effect. It MUST NOT block or roll back the database move transaction. If the messaging service is unavailable, revocation failures are logged and swallowed (fire-and-forget pattern). No application-level retry is performed; transport-level reliability (AMQP message durability) provides best-effort delivery.
+- **FR-009**: After membership revocation, former members MUST NOT be able to post new messages to any room in the moved space.
+

+# Feature Specification: Matrix Space Lifecycle Management
+
+**Feature Branch**: `082-matrix-space-lifecycle`
+**Created**: 2026-03-25
+**Status**: Draft
+**Input**: User description: "Add space lifecycle management in the matrix - maintain hierarchy of matrix spaces mirroring Alkemio spaces, anchor rooms to corresponding matrix spaces, handle create/update/delete/relocate lifecycle events, and manage forum discussion hierarchy (forum->category->room)."
+
+## Clarifications
+
+### Session 2026-03-25
+
+- Q: Should the system backfill Matrix spaces for existing Alkemio spaces? → A: No automatic backfill. Provide an idempotent admin GQL mutation to synchronize existing spaces into Matrix hierarchy on demand. Must be safe to run multiple times.
+- Q: What does "publicly readable/writable" mean for forum rooms? → A: Any authenticated user on the Alkemio Synapse server can read and write (joinable without invitation). Targeted at users accessing Matrix via Element. Not open to anonymous/guest or federated users.
+- Q: Should Matrix spaces (containers) also be visible to all Synapse users? → A: Only forum and category Matrix spaces are visible/joinable by all Synapse users. Alkemio space containers require invitation (membership management deferred to a future PR).
+
+## User Scenarios & Testing _(mandatory)_
+
+### User Story 1 - Space Creation Mirrors to Matrix (Priority: P1)
+
+When a platform administrator or space host creates a new top-level space or subspace in Alkemio, a corresponding Matrix space is automatically created and anchored to the correct parent in the Matrix hierarchy.
+
+**Why this priority**: This is the foundational capability. Without creating Matrix spaces, no hierarchy can exist, and rooms cannot be organized.
+
+**Independent Test**: Create a top-level space in Alkemio and verify a corresponding Matrix space is created. Create a subspace and verify it is created and anchored under the parent Matrix space.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** no existing Matrix space for a new Alkemio space, **When** a top-level space is created in Alkemio, **Then** a corresponding Matrix space is created with the space's display name.
+2. **Given** a parent Alkemio space with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** a subspace is created under that parent, **Then** a Matrix space is created for the subspace AND it is anchored as a child of the parent's Matrix space.
+3. **Given** a deeply nested subspace hierarchy (e.g., Space > Subspace > Sub-subspace), **When** the deepest subspace is created, **Then** the Matrix hierarchy correctly reflects the full nesting chain.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 2 - Room Anchoring to Matrix Spaces (Priority: P1)
+
+When any room (updates, callout comments, posts, conversations) is created under an Alkemio space or subspace, that room is automatically anchored to the corresponding Matrix space in the hierarchy.
+
+**Why this priority**: Rooms are the primary communication artifacts. Anchoring them to Matrix spaces is essential for the hierarchy to have practical value.
+
+**Independent Test**: Create a room (e.g., updates room) under a space that has a corresponding Matrix space, and verify the room is anchored as a child of that Matrix space.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a space with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** an updates room is created for that space, **Then** the room is anchored as a child of the Matrix space.
+2. **Given** a subspace with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** a callout room is created under that subspace, **Then** the room is anchored to the subspace's Matrix space (not the parent space's).
+3. **Given** a space whose Matrix space does not yet exist (e.g., created before this feature), **When** a room is created under that space, **Then** the system handles the missing Matrix space gracefully (creates it on-demand or skips anchoring without error).
+
+---
+
+### User Story 3 - Forum Discussion Hierarchy in Matrix (Priority: P2)
+
+When forum discussions are created under a space, the system maintains a Matrix space hierarchy of forum (Matrix space) -> category (Matrix space) -> room, mirroring the Alkemio forum structure.
+
+**Why this priority**: Forums have a richer hierarchical structure than simple rooms. This extends the hierarchy concept to cover the full communication model.
+
+**Independent Test**: Create a forum discussion under a category in a space's forum, and verify the Matrix hierarchy shows: Space (Matrix space) > Forum (Matrix space) > Category (Matrix space) > Discussion Room.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a space with a Matrix space, **When** a forum discussion is created, **Then** Matrix spaces for the forum and category are created (if not already existing) and the discussion room is anchored under the category Matrix space.
+2. **Given** an existing forum Matrix space hierarchy, **When** a new discussion is added to an existing category, **Then** only the discussion room is created and anchored; the forum and category Matrix spaces are reused.
+3. **Given** a new category is created in an existing forum, **When** a discussion is created under it, **Then** a new category Matrix space is created under the forum Matrix space, and the discussion room is anchored under it.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 4 - Space Display Name and Avatar Sync to Matrix (Priority: P2)
+
+When the display name or avatar of an Alkemio space or subspace is updated, the corresponding Matrix space name and avatar are also updated. When a space is first created with an avatar, the Matrix space receives that avatar.
+
+**Why this priority**: Keeps naming and visual identity consistent across systems, important for usability but not blocking for the core hierarchy.
+
+**Independent Test**: Update the display name of a space in Alkemio and verify the Matrix space name is updated. Upload or change a space avatar and verify the Matrix space avatar is updated accordingly.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a space with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** the space's display name is changed, **Then** the Matrix space name is updated to match.
+2. **Given** a subspace with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** the subspace's display name is changed, **Then** the Matrix space name is updated.
+3. **Given** a space with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** the space's avatar is uploaded or changed, **Then** the Matrix space avatar is updated to match.
+4. **Given** a space with an avatar is created, **When** the corresponding Matrix space is created, **Then** the Matrix space is initialized with the space's avatar.
+5. **Given** a space with a corresponding Matrix space, **When** the space's avatar is removed, **Then** the Matrix space avatar is also removed.
+6. **Given** the Matrix adapter is unavailable, **When** a space display name or avatar is updated, **Then** the Alkemio update succeeds and the Matrix update failure is logged without blocking the operation.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 5 - Space Deletion Cascades to Matrix (Priority: P2)
+
+When a space or subspace is deleted in Alkemio, the corresponding Matrix space and all rooms beneath it in the Matrix hierarchy are also deleted.
+
+**Why this priority**: Prevents orphaned Matrix spaces and rooms from accumulating. Important for hygiene but less frequent than creation.
+
+**Independent Test**: Delete a space that has a corresponding Matrix space with child rooms, and verify the Matrix space and its children are removed.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a space with a corresponding Matrix space and child rooms, **When** the space is deleted, **Then** the Matrix space and all its child rooms/spaces are deleted.
+2. **Given** a parent space with subspaces, **When** the parent space is deleted, **Then** the entire Matrix subtree (parent space, subspaces, and all rooms) is removed.
+3. **Given** a space whose Matrix space has already been deleted externally, **When** the space is deleted in Alkemio, **Then** the operation completes without error.
+
+---
+

+5. **Given** forum hierarchies exist, **When** the sync mutation runs, **Then** forum and category Matrix spaces are created and discussion rooms are anchored with public read/write visibility.

+

+- **FR-003**: System MUST update the Matrix space display name when the corresponding Alkemio space display name is changed.
+- **FR-013**: System MUST set the Matrix space avatar when creating a Matrix space for an Alkemio space that has an avatar.
+- **FR-014**: System MUST update the Matrix space avatar when the corresponding Alkemio space avatar is changed or removed.
+- **FR-004**: System MUST delete the Matrix space (and all child rooms/spaces beneath it) when the corresponding Alkemio space is deleted.
+- **FR-005**: System MUST re-anchor a Matrix space under a new parent when the corresponding Alkemio space is relocated.
+- **FR-006**: System MUST anchor any newly created room to its owning space's Matrix space in the hierarchy.
+- **FR-007**: System MUST create and maintain a Matrix space hierarchy for forums: forum (Matrix space) -> category (Matrix space) -> discussion room.
+- **FR-011**: System MUST create all rooms within the forum hierarchy (forum > category > discussion room) as readable and writable by any authenticated user on the Alkemio Synapse server (joinable without invitation, not open to anonymous or federated users).
+- **FR-012**: System MUST NOT apply public visibility settings to non-forum rooms (updates, callout, conversation rooms) when anchoring them to Matrix spaces.
+- **FR-017**: Forum and category Matrix spaces MUST be visible and joinable by all authenticated Synapse server users.
+- **FR-018**: Alkemio space container Matrix spaces MUST require invitation to join (membership management is out of scope for this feature and deferred to a future PR).

+# Feature Specification: Change User Login Email With Ownership Verification
+
+**Feature Branch**: `097-change-user-email`
+**Created**: 2026-05-13
+**Status**: Draft
+**Input**: User description: "implement https://github.com/orgs/alkem-io/projects/50/views/8?pane=issue&itemId=187119757&issue=alkem-io%7Cserver%7C6064"
+
+**Related Issues**:
+
+- alkem-io/server#6064 — Allow changing a user's login email while preserving their Alkemio profile
+
+## User Scenarios & Testing _(mandatory)_
+
+### User Story 1 — User Changes Their Own Login Email (Priority: P1)
+
+As a registered Alkemio user, I want to change the email address I use to log in so that I can move authentication to a new mailbox (e.g., after a job change or provider migration) without losing my profile, memberships, contributions, or history.
+
+**Why this priority**: This is the primary user-facing capability the feature exists to deliver. Without it, users have no self-service path to update their login email, and the platform falls back to ad-hoc database edits that have already drifted out of sync with the identity provider.
+
+**Independent Test**: A logged-in user requests an email change to a new address, confirms ownership via the email sent to that new address, and is then able to log in only with the new address — the old address no longer authenticates. The user's profile id, memberships, and content remain unchanged.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a logged-in user with a valid login email, **When** the user requests to change their email to a new, unused address, **Then** the platform sends a confirmation message to the new address and records a pending change without yet altering the login email.
+2. **Given** a pending email change with an unexpired confirmation token, **When** the user proves ownership of the new address (clicks the confirmation link in the message sent to that address), **Then** the login email is updated in both the Alkemio user record and the identity provider, the user's profile id is unchanged, and the pending change is marked complete.
+3. **Given** the user has completed the change, **When** they attempt to log in with the new address, **Then** authentication succeeds; **When** they attempt to log in with the old address, **Then** authentication is rejected.
+4. **Given** the user has completed the change, **When** they view their profile, **Then** all memberships, contributions, and historical references are intact and continue to reference the same user identity.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 2 — Platform Admin Changes a User's Login Email On Their Behalf (Priority: P1)
+
+As a platform administrator, I want to initiate an email change for another user (e.g., when the user has lost access to their old mailbox and contacts support) so that I can restore their access while still requiring proof that they control the new mailbox.
+
+**Why this priority**: Admin-on-behalf-of is a primary support flow. Many email-change requests arrive precisely because the user can no longer access the old address; the user therefore cannot initiate a self-service flow from within Alkemio. Without this path, support has no way to resolve the case except by editing the database, which is exactly what this feature replaces.
+
+**Independent Test**: A platform admin initiates an email change for another user's account, the confirmation message is sent to the proposed new address, and once the target user confirms ownership, the change is committed across both systems. The action is recorded in the audit trail with the admin's identity, the target user's identity, the old address, and the new address.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a platform admin acting on behalf of another user, **When** the admin initiates an email change for that user with a new address, **Then** the platform validates the new address (format + uniqueness) and sends a confirmation message to it, recording a pending change attributed to the admin.
+2. **Given** the pending admin-initiated change, **When** the target user confirms ownership via the confirmation message, **Then** the change is committed across the Alkemio user record and the identity provider, and an audit entry is recorded that captures the actor (admin), the subject (user), the old address, and the new address.
+3. **Given** a non-admin user, **When** they attempt to initiate an email change for someone else, **Then** the platform rejects the request with an authorization error and no message is sent.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 3 — Atomic Two-Side Commit With Rollback on Partial Failure (Priority: P1)
+
+As a platform operator, I want the email change to either fully succeed across both Alkemio and the identity provider or fully fail with no partial state, so that the two systems cannot silently drift out of sync the way they did under the legacy database-edit approach.
+
+**Why this priority**: Drift between the Alkemio user record and the identity provider is the root failure mode the issue exists to fix. Even a perfect verification flow is unsafe if a mid-commit failure leaves Alkemio updated but the identity provider unchanged (or vice versa). Without this guarantee, the feature reintroduces the very problem it was created to solve.
+
+**Independent Test**: Simulate a failure on the second-side write (e.g., the identity provider is unreachable or returns an error) after the first side has been updated, and verify that the first-side change is rolled back so the user's login email is unchanged on both sides. A clear error is surfaced to the initiator.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a confirmed pending change, **When** the platform updates the Alkemio user record successfully but the identity provider write fails, **Then** the platform reverses the Alkemio update so both sides reflect the old email, and surfaces a clear error to the initiator.
+2. **Given** a confirmed pending change, **When** the identity provider write succeeds but persisting the Alkemio user record fails, **Then** the platform reverses the identity provider update so both sides reflect the old email, and surfaces a clear error to the initiator.
+3. **Given** any partial-failure recovery has run, **When** the user next attempts to log in, **Then** the old email continues to work (the system is in its pre-change state), and the user can retry the change.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 4 — Confirmation Token Lifecycle (Priority: P2)
+
+As a security-conscious platform, I want confirmation tokens to be short-lived, single-use, and bound to the specific (user, proposed new email) pair, so that a leaked or replayed token cannot be used to hijack an account or to redirect a different user's email change.
+
+**Why this priority**: The verification token is the only thing standing between an initiator and a committed email change. Without strict lifecycle rules, leaked links and stale tokens become a credible attack surface. P2 because the underlying flow (P1 stories) is what the user sees; this story is what makes the flow safe to operate.
+
+**Independent Test**: Issue a confirmation token, then attempt to use it (a) twice, (b) for a different user, (c) after expiry, and (d) after the user has initiated a newer change. Each MUST be rejected with a clear error, and no email change MUST be committed.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** an unused confirmation token, **When** the user confirms ownership before the token expires, **Then** the change proceeds and the token is marked consumed.
+2. **Given** a confirmation token that has already been consumed, **When** the same token is presented again, **Then** the platform rejects it and surfaces a clear "already used" error.
+3. **Given** a confirmation token that has expired, **When** the user attempts to confirm, **Then** the platform rejects it and surfaces a clear "expired" error, optionally inviting the user to restart the change.
+4. **Given** an outstanding pending change for a user, **When** the same user (or admin) initiates a new email change for that user, **Then** the previous token is invalidated and only the new token is honored.
+
+---
+
+### User Story 5 — Conflict and Validation Errors Before Sending Mail (Priority: P2)
+
+As any initiator of an email change, I want to be told immediately when the proposed new address is invalid or already in use, so that no confirmation mail is sent to an address that could never be assigned.
+
+**Why this priority**: Validation before sending mail prevents accidental disclosure (sending a confirmation to an address that belongs to a different user), reduces spam complaints, and gives the initiator immediate feedback. P2 because the system would still be correct if uniqueness were only enforced on commit, but the user experience and abuse posture are materially worse.
+
+**Independent Test**: Submit an email change with (a) a malformed address, (b) the user's current address, and (c) an address already belonging to another Alkemio user or identity provider identity. Each MUST be rejected before any mail is sent.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a malformed new email address, **When** the change is requested, **Then** the platform rejects with a validation error and does not send mail.
+2. **Given** a new email identical to the user's current login email, **When** the change is requested, **Then** the platform rejects with a "no change" error and does not send mail.
+3. **Given** a new email already in use by another Alkemio user or identity provider identity, **When** the change is requested, **Then** the platform rejects with a "conflict" error and does not send mail, and the error MUST NOT confirm or deny which user owns the conflicting address (to avoid enumeration).
+
+---
+
+### User Story 6 — Audit Trail of Email Changes (Priority: P3)
+
+As a platform operator (and, for the user's own benefit, as the user themselves), I want every successful email change recorded with who initiated it, who the subject was, the old address, the new address, and when it happened, so that we can investigate incidents and answer "did anyone touch this account?" later.
+
+**Why this priority**: Audit logging is critical for security investigations and for support, but the system is functional without it; therefore P3. It MUST land with the feature, not retrofitted.
+
+**Independent Test**: After any successful email change (self- or admin-initiated), an audit entry is retrievable that includes initiator, subject, old address, new address, timestamp, and outcome. Failed attempts (rejected validation, expired token, partial-failure rollback) also produce entries with the failure reason.
+
+**Acceptance Scenarios**:
+
+1. **Given** a successfully committed email change, **When** the audit log is queried, **Then** an entry exists with initiator, subject, old address, new address, timestamp, and outcome = success.
+2. **Given** a partial-failure rollback, **When** the audit log is queried, **Then** an entry exists describing the failure, the side(s) on which it occurred, and that both sides were restored.
+3. **Given** a rejected attempt (validation, conflict, expired/used token), **When** the audit log is queried, **Then** an entry exists describing the rejection reason without leaking sensitive details (e.g., the existence of conflicting accounts).
+
+---
+
+### Edge Cases
+
+- The user's old mailbox is already unreachable when the change is initiated. The self-service path requires login but not access to the old mailbox; the admin-on-behalf path explicitly supports this case.
+- The user requests a change, then immediately requests another change to a different address before confirming the first. The system MUST invalidate the prior pending token and accept only the most recent one.
+- The user clicks the confirmation link in a different browser / device than where they initiated the change. The confirmation MUST succeed regardless of session continuity, because the token is the proof of ownership; no session binding is required for the confirmation step itself.
+- The user confirms but their Alkemio session has expired in the meantime. The confirmation MUST still commit the change (the token, not the session, is the authority for the confirmation step).
+- The new email is identical (case-insensitive) to the current email. The platform MUST treat addresses case-insensitively for equality and conflict checks.
+- The identity provider returns a non-error but unexpected response shape (e.g., the identity id no longer exists). The platform MUST treat this as a failure of the commit and trigger rollback rather than recording success.
+- Two confirmations arrive simultaneously (e.g., the user clicks the link twice in quick succession). The platform MUST commit exactly once and reject the second attempt as "already used".
+- The user is in a partial-failure rollback state when they retry. The retry MUST succeed normally, as the system was returned to its pre-change state.
+- The pending change exists for a user whose Alkemio account is subsequently deactivated or deleted before confirmation. The token MUST be rejected on confirmation and the pending change cleaned up.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Changing identity-provider-managed credentials other than the email trait (password, MFA factors, OIDC links).
+- Changing the user's display name, contact preferences, or any non-login email fields. The Alkemio user has one login email; other addresses (if any) are not affected.
+- Bulk admin email-change operations (migrating many users at once). Each change MUST go through the verified per-user flow.
+- A client-side UI for the flow. This specification covers the server-side capability; the client experience (initiation form, confirmation landing page, admin console entry point) is handled in client-web and is referenced only where the server contract constrains it.
+
+## Requirements _(mandatory)_
+
+### Functional Requirements
+
+- **FR-001**: System MUST expose a server-side capability for a logged-in user to initiate a change to their own login email.
+- **FR-002**: System MUST expose a server-side capability for a platform administrator to initiate a login-email change on behalf of any other user.
+- **FR-002a**: The email-change capability (FR-001 and FR-002) MUST be available for any Kratos identity regardless of credential type (password credential, OIDC link, or both). The `email` trait change is applied identically in all cases; OIDC link bookkeeping is not modified (consistent with the existing Out of Scope declaration). OIDC-only users MUST NOT be rejected at initiation on the basis that they lack a Kratos password credential.
+- **FR-003**: System MUST require proof of ownership of the proposed new email before committing the change on either side. Proof is established by the user (or, in the admin-on-behalf case, the target user) demonstrating control of the new mailbox via a confirmation message sent to that address.
+- **FR-003a**: The confirmation message MUST contain a clickable link whose target carries an opaque single-use token. The link MUST target a client-web URL (the client application's deep link for confirming an email change), NOT a server-side HTTP endpoint; the client-web app reads the token from the URL and invokes the GraphQL confirm mutation. The server MUST NOT introduce a new HTTP route to consume the token directly; all confirmation logic remains behind the GraphQL surface. Confirmation MUST be reachable solely by following that link; the feature MUST NOT additionally emit a user-typeable code, and the confirm mutation MUST accept a single token string (no separate code-based code path).
+- **FR-003b**: The confirmation message body MUST contain, in addition to the clickable link from FR-003a: (a) the initiator role tag (`self` vs `platform admin`) so the recipient understands whether the change was initiated by them or by an administrator acting on their behalf, (b) an explicit statement that the link is time-limited and consistent with the 1-hour TTL contracted in FR-007b (exact wording is an implementation choice, but the message MUST convey time-bound urgency rather than leaving expiry unstated), and (c) a recovery / disclaimer line instructing the recipient to ignore the message and contact support if the change was not expected. The message MUST NOT include: the initiating admin's display name, user id, or other admin PII (only the role tag is permitted — this is intentionally narrower than the FR-022 admin-profile disclosure, because the new-mailbox recipient may be a third party at the moment of read); the confirmation token outside the link itself; the identity provider identity id; or any other internal identifier. The message MUST be rendered in English per FR-016a; no per-user locale resolution is introduced. The trust-signal pattern (role tag + expiry + recovery instructions) intentionally mirrors FR-016's content contract for the post-commit security-signal notification at the old address.
+- **FR-004**: System MUST validate the proposed new email's format and its uniqueness across both the Alkemio user records and the identity provider's identities before sending any confirmation message.
+- **FR-004a**: System MUST re-validate the proposed new email's uniqueness at confirmation time, before any side-write to either Alkemio or the identity provider. The re-check applies the same scope as FR-004 (Alkemio user records and identity provider identities) and the same case-insensitivity rules from FR-006. If the proposed email is now in use by another Alkemio user or identity provider identity, the confirmation MUST be rejected with a `conflict` error (per FR-015), no side-write MUST occur on either side, and an audit entry with the `conflict` rejection outcome MUST be written (subject to the non-leaky failure-reason rules of FR-014 — the entry MUST NOT confirm or deny which user owns the conflicting address). The pending-change record MUST NOT transition to `confirmed` or `committed` in this case; supersession by a new initiation (per FR-007(d) and FR-019) remains the user's path forward. This narrows the window in which the FR-009 compensating-rollback path would otherwise be exercised for a benign uniqueness race between initiation and confirmation, while preserving the FR-009 guarantee for genuine commit-time failures.
+- **FR-005**: System MUST reject a proposed new email that equals (case-insensitively) the user's current login email with a "no change" error, and MUST NOT send a confirmation message in that case.
+- **FR-006**: System MUST treat email addresses case-insensitively for equality and conflict checks, while preserving the original casing supplied by the user for display.
+- **FR-007**: System MUST issue confirmation tokens that are (a) short-lived, (b) single-use, (c) scoped to the specific user and the specific proposed new email, and (d) invalidated when a newer pending change is initiated for the same user.
+- **FR-007a**: The confirmation token MUST be persisted as plaintext on the pending-change record (no separate hash column). Confirmation lookups compare the presented token against the stored plaintext value directly. The token's safety relies on (i) its short TTL (per FR-007(a) and the concrete value in FR-007b), (ii) its single-use semantics (FR-007(b)), (iii) the invalidation rule on supersession (FR-007(d)), (iv) database access controls applied to the pending-change record, and (v) its entropy floor (per FR-007c). Audit entries (FR-014/FR-014a) MUST NOT contain the token value.
+- **FR-007c**: The confirmation token MUST be generated from a cryptographically secure random source and MUST carry at least 128 bits of entropy. The token's serialized form MUST be URL-safe (e.g., base64url or hex) so that it can be embedded as a query-string parameter in the client-web deep link defined in FR-003a without further encoding. The serialized form's character length is an implementation choice subject to the 128-bit floor (e.g., 22+ characters of base64url, or 32+ characters of hex). The token MUST NOT encode or derive from the subject user id, the proposed new email, the issue timestamp, or any other identifier — it is an opaque random value, and the binding to the (user, proposed new email) pair is established by the pending-change record, not by the token's internal structure. The 128-bit entropy floor is a contract surface; raising it (e.g., to 256 bits) is permissible without a spec change, but lowering it MUST be treated as a spec-level decision.
+- **FR-007b**: The confirmation token's TTL MUST be exactly 1 hour from its issue timestamp. The 1-hour TTL applies uniformly to both self-initiated and admin-initiated changes — the platform MUST NOT introduce a tiered TTL keyed on initiator role. Tokens presented after the 1-hour boundary MUST be rejected per FR-007(a) and FR-008 and MUST surface the expired-token error per FR-015. The same 1-hour expiry MUST be the value materialized in the pending-change record's `expiryTimestamp` field returned by FR-022. The TTL is a contract surface; changing it is a spec-level decision, not an environment-level configuration.
+- **FR-008**: System MUST consume the confirmation token atomically: a successful confirmation triggers the two-side commit; a failed or rejected confirmation MUST NOT alter the login email on either side.
+- **FR-009**: System MUST commit the email change such that, in effect, either both the Alkemio user record and the identity provider identity reflect the new email, or neither does. Before declaring a side write a failure, the platform MUST perform a bounded synchronous retry with backoff against the identity provider (small number of attempts, total budget on the order of 5–10 seconds) to absorb transient errors. Once the retry budget is exhausted, the failure MUST be treated as terminal and trigger a compensating action that returns both sides to the pre-change state. Background / asynchronous reconciliation MUST NOT be used to defer commit beyond the synchronous budget.
+- **FR-009a**: The compensating rollback (FR-009) MUST itself observe the same bounded synchronous retry budget (2–3 attempts, total budget ~5–10 seconds) when calling the failing side. If the rollback retry budget is exhausted without restoring the pre-change state, the system MUST: (a) transition the pending change to the terminal state `drift_detected` (a seventh state added to the FR-021 enumeration), (b) write an audit entry with outcome `drift_detected` capturing the observed values on each side and the failure reason, (c) surface a distinct error to the initiator clearly identifying that drift remains and that admin-driven reconciliation is required (per FR-009b), and (d) emit an operations-alert signal via the existing observability channels — specifically, a Winston error-level log entry **and** an Elastic APM error capture, both tagged with a known event marker (e.g., `email_change_drift_detected`) so existing log-based and APM-based alerting can fire on it. No new ops-alert infrastructure (e.g., dedicated RabbitMQ queue, webhook, or paging integration) is introduced by this feature. No asynchronous / background reconciler is introduced; reconciliation of a `drift_detected` pending change is an admin-driven synchronous operation invoked via the dedicated mutation defined in FR-009b, preserving the FR-009 guardrail against background reconciliation.
+- **FR-009b**: When a pending email change is in the `drift_detected` terminal state (per FR-009a), reconciliation MUST be performed via a dedicated `platformAdmin` GraphQL mutation introduced by this feature (e.g., `platformAdminResolveEmailChangeDrift`), and NOT via direct PostgreSQL edits or direct Kratos admin-console operations. The mutation MUST take a single `Input` object identifying the subject user and the admin-chosen canonical email; the canonical email MUST be one of the two values observed on the `drift_detected` record (i.e., the admin's choice is "keep the change" vs "revert the change"). The mutation MUST read current values on both sides, apply alignment writes only where needed, and observe the same bounded synchronous retry budget as FR-009 (2–3 attempts, total ~5–10 seconds per side that requires a write). On successful alignment, an audit entry with outcome `drift_resolved` MUST be written capturing actor, subject, canonical email selected, prior observed values per side, and timestamp. On failure to align within the retry budget, the mutation MUST surface a distinct error and write an audit entry with outcome `drift_resolution_failed`; the pending-change record MUST remain in `drift_detected`. The `drift_detected` pending-change record itself MUST NOT transition state on successful resolution; it remains as forensic evidence (and is purged on the same 30-day window per FR-020, while the audit entries persist indefinitely per FR-014a).
+- **FR-010**: System MUST update the identity provider's existing identity in place (same identity id). The Alkemio user's profile id and identity provider identity id MUST NOT change as a result of the email change; memberships, contributions, and historical references MUST remain associated with the same user.
+- **FR-011**: System MUST mark the new email as verified on the identity provider side at commit time, so that the user is not prompted to re-verify the address after the change.
+- **FR-012**: After a successful change, the system MUST allow login with the new email and MUST reject login attempts using the old email.
+- **FR-013**: System MUST authorize the initiation endpoint such that a user MAY initiate a change only for themselves, and a platform administrator MAY initiate a change for any user. Other actors MUST be rejected with an authorization error.
+- **FR-014**: System MUST record an audit entry for every initiation, every confirmation outcome (success, rejection, expiry), and every rollback, capturing initiator, subject, old address, new address, timestamp, and outcome. Audit entries MUST NOT leak the existence of conflicting accounts in their failure-reason fields.
+- **FR-014a**: Audit entries MUST be persisted in a dedicated entity introduced by this feature (e.g., `email_change_audit_entry`) backed by PostgreSQL, so that they remain queryable beyond the 30-day pending-change retention window (FR-020) and so that events with no corresponding pending-change record (validation rejection before persistence; initiation rolled back under FR-019a) still have a durable home. The codebase has no pre-existing general-purpose audit entity to extend, so this entity is new. The existing `activity-log` infrastructure (user-facing collaboration activity feed) MUST NOT be reused for this purpose. Structured Winston log entries MAY be emitted in parallel for operational visibility but MUST NOT be treated as the system of record; the dedicated entity is the system of record per FR-020. Audit entries MUST be retained indefinitely; this feature MUST NOT introduce an automatic purge or retention window for `email_change_audit_entry`. Removal of audit entries for a deleted subject user is delegated to the platform's existing user-deletion workflow and is out of scope here.
+- **FR-014b**: System MUST expose a paginated GraphQL query under the `platformAdmin` surface that returns the `email_change_audit_entry` records for a given subject user, ordered by timestamp descending. The query MUST be keyed by subject user only; additional filters (by initiator, outcome, or date range) are out of scope for this iteration. The query MUST follow the project's pagination conventions (`docs/Pagination.md`). Returned fields MUST include: (a) `initiator` as a minimal user profile summary `{ id, displayName }` (matching the FR-022 pattern), (b) `initiatorRole` as a tag (`self` vs `platform admin`) distinguishing self-initiated from admin-on-behalf entries, (c) `subject` as a minimal user profile summary `{ id, displayName }`, (d) old address, (e) new address, (f) timestamp, (g) outcome (from the audit-outcome enumeration introduced by this feature — `initiated`, `confirmed`, `committed`, `rolled_back`, `expired`, `superseded`, `drift_detected`, `drift_resolved`, `drift_resolution_failed`, `initiation_failed`, `security_signal_failed`, `session_invalidation_failed`, plus rejection outcomes for validation/conflict/used-token/expired-token presentations — the planning artifact MUST enumerate the final canonical set), and (h) where applicable, the non-leaky failure reason. The query MUST NOT expose the confirmation token; MUST NOT expose the initiator's or subject's email address or any other PII beyond `id` and `displayName`; MUST NOT return any field that has been redacted or masked elsewhere in the feature (the old/new addresses on the audit entry are the canonical addresses observed at the moment the entry was written, not the FR-016 masked form). For entries whose `initiator` cannot be resolved to a profile summary (e.g., validation-rejection entries written before the initiator's identity was fully resolved per FR-014a), the planning artifact MUST define a sentinel representation; the `initiatorRole` tag MUST always be present. No `me`-shaped audit query is introduced for the calling user in this iteration; users observe their own active pending change via FR-022 and the post-commit security-signal notification via FR-016.
+- **FR-015**: System MUST surface clear, distinct errors for each failure mode (identity provider unreachable, identity provider write failed, Alkemio write failed, conflict, expired token, used token, invalid format, "no change") without leaking sensitive internals.

_🛠️ Refactor suggestion_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Clarify the PII constraint in FR-014b to avoid confusion between audit values and current user emails.**

FR-014b states the query "MUST NOT expose the initiator's or subject's email address" but earlier in the same requirement mandates returning "(d) old address, (e) new address". This phrasing is ambiguous: does "subject's email address" mean the subject's *current* email (which could differ from the audited old/new values after subsequent changes), or does it mean the old/new emails captured in the audit entry?

The intent (per plan.md line 36) appears to be: audit entries store and return `old_email`/`new_email` for forensic purposes, but the GraphQL response does NOT include separate fields for the initiator's or subject's *current* email addresses (only their `{id, displayName}`). However, the current phrasing conflates these.




<details>
<summary>✏️ Proposed clarification</summary>

```diff
-FR-014b: ... Returned fields MUST include: (a) `initiator` as a minimal user profile summary `{ id, displayName }`, (b) `initiatorRole` as a tag (`self` vs `platform admin`) distinguishing self-initiated (when spec 098 lands) from admin-on-behalf entries — this spec only writes `platform admin`, (c) `subject` as a minimal user profile summary `{ id, displayName }`, (d) old address, (e) new address, (f) timestamp, (g) outcome (from the audit-outcome enumeration introduced by this feature), and (h) where applicable, the non-leaky failure reason. The query MUST NOT expose the initiator's or subject's email address or any other PII beyond `id` and `displayName`.
+FR-014b: ... Returned fields MUST include: (a) `initiator` as a minimal user profile summary `{ id, displayName }`, (b) `initiatorRole` as a tag (`self` vs `platform admin`) distinguishing self-initiated (when spec 098 lands) from admin-on-behalf entries — this spec only writes `platform admin`, (c) `subject` as a minimal user profile summary `{ id, displayName }`, (d) the audited old email address from the change event, (e) the audited new email address from the change event, (f) timestamp, (g) outcome (from the audit-outcome enumeration introduced by this feature), and (h) where applicable, the non-leaky failure reason. The `initiator` and `subject` profile summaries MUST NOT include email addresses or any other PII beyond `id` and `displayName`; the only email addresses returned are the audited old/new values captured at the time of the change.
```

This rephrasing makes clear that:
1. The audit query returns the historical old/new email values (forensic record).
2. The initiator/subject profile summaries exclude current email addresses.
3. No ambiguity about "subject's email address".

</details>

+
+**Feature Branch**: `097-change-user-email`
+**Created**: 2026-05-13
+**Last Updated**: 2026-05-18 (smaller MVP — email-ownership verification moved to spec 098)

This trade-off is acceptable here because (a) the admin already takes responsibility for the manual verification per current support practice, (b) the immediate ask of the issue is to stop the direct database edits — not to replace the support process with platform-mediated verification, and (c) the post-commit security-signal notification at the **old** address still gives the original user the opportunity to detect and escalate an erroneous or malicious change. The self-service flow in spec 098 introduces the full platform-mediated verification path for the case where no admin is in the loop and ownership of the new mailbox MUST be proven by the platform.

+
+### User Story 1 — Platform Admin Changes a User's Login Email On Their Behalf (Priority: P1)
+
+As a platform administrator, I want to change the login email of another user (e.g., when the user has lost access to their old mailbox and contacts support) so that I can restore their access without resorting to direct database edits, while remaining accountable in the audit trail.
+
+**Why this priority**: This is the only user-facing capability in this spec. It is the support flow that replaces the ad-hoc database edits that motivated this feature. The admin is expected to have verified the user's identity out-of-band before invoking this capability.

The change is observable end-to-end without any direct database edits. The user can subsequently log in only with the new address; the old address no longer authenticates.
+

+
+1. **Given** a platform admin acting on behalf of another user, **When** the admin invokes the email-change mutation with a new address, **Then** the platform validates the new address (format + uniqueness) and, if validation passes, commits the change on both the Alkemio user record and the identity provider in a single synchronous operation, recording the action in the audit trail.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Add an explicit gate: block new admin changes while unresolved drift exists.**

FR-009b defines how drift is resolved, but it doesn’t explicitly require `adminUserEmailChange` to reject when latest audit state is unresolved `drift_detected`. Please codify this guard and expected error (e.g., `DRIFT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED`) to prevent compounding inconsistencies.  
 

As per coding guidelines, “Speckit specs capture the constitution for behaviour. Confirm changes satisfy acceptance criteria, update impacted requirements, and flag any divergence or missing traceability.”


Also applies to: 129-129

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against current code. Fix only still-valid issues, skip the
rest with a brief reason, keep changes minimal, and validate.

In `@specs/097-change-user-email/spec.md` at line 121, Add an explicit guard in
the admin email-change flow so adminUserEmailChange rejects when the subject's
most recent audit outcome is drift_detected and no subsequent drift_resolved
exists: before performing any writes, read the latest audit row for the subject
and if outcome == "drift_detected" (and not followed by "drift_resolved") return
a distinct error (e.g., DRIFT_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED) and do not proceed;
reference the new reconciliation mutation adminUserEmailChangeDriftResolve for
resolution and ensure the original drift_detected audit row is left untouched.
```

</details>

+### User Story 1 — Platform Admin Changes a User's Login Email On Their Behalf (Priority: P1)

+As a platform administrator, I want to change the login email of another user (e.g., when the user has lost access to their old mailbox and contacts support) so that I can restore their access without resorting to direct database edits, while remaining accountable in the audit trail.

The platform validates the new address (format + uniqueness), commits the change on both the Alkemio user record and the identity provider in a single synchronous operation, invalidates the user's existing identity-provider sessions, sends a security-signal notification to the **old** address, and records every step in the audit trail. +

+1. **Given** a platform admin acting on behalf of another user, **When** the admin invokes the email-change mutation with a new address, **Then** the platform validates the new address (format + uniqueness) and, if validation passes, commits the change on both the Alkemio user record and the identity provider in a single synchronous operation, recording the action in the audit trail.

+3. **Given** the change has committed, **When** the subject views their profile, **Then** all memberships, contributions, and historical references are intact and continue to reference the same user identity.
+4. **Given** a non-admin user, **When** they attempt to invoke the email-change mutation for someone else, **Then** the platform rejects the request with an authorization error and no change occurs.
+5. **Given** the change has committed, **When** the audit log is queried for the subject, **Then** the admin's identity, the subject's identity, the old address, the new address, the timestamp, and a `committed` outcome are recorded.

+---
+

+As a platform operator, I want the email change to either fully succeed across both Alkemio and the identity provider or fully fail with no partial state, so that the two systems cannot silently drift out of sync the way they did under the legacy database-edit approach.

Without this guarantee, the feature reintroduces the very problem it was created to solve.

+As an admin initiator of an email change, I want to be told immediately when the proposed new address is invalid or already in use, so that no change is attempted on a target value that could never be assigned.

+2. **Given** a partial-failure rollback, **When** the audit log is queried, **Then** an entry exists with outcome = `rolled_back` and a non-leaky failure reason describing the side(s) on which the failure occurred.

+
+This feature introduces **one** entity:
+
+- **Audit Entry** (`email_change_audit_entry`): An append-only record describing one step in the email-change lifecycle (commit, rollback, drift detection, drift resolution, drift-resolution failure, security-signal failure, session-invalidation failure, validation rejection, conflict rejection) with initiator, subject, old address, new address, timestamp, outcome, and a non-leaky failure reason where applicable. Persisted in PostgreSQL. Retained indefinitely (no purge by this feature; per-subject removal is delegated to the platform user-deletion workflow). Independent of any pre-existing audit / activity-log infrastructure. For drift-detected entries, `old_email` records the value observed on the Alkemio side at the moment of drift and `new_email` records the value observed on the identity-provider side (consistent with the Kratos-first commit ordering: at drift, Alkemio holds its old value because that write never started, and Kratos holds the new value because its write succeeded but the revert failed).
+
+**Note**: This spec does NOT introduce a `pending` entity. There is no multi-step lifecycle; the admin mutation is a single synchronous call. Spec 098 introduces `email_change_pending` natively as part of its verification flow.
+
+## Success Criteria _(mandatory)_
+
+### Measurable Outcomes
+
+- **SC-001**: A platform administrator can complete an admin-on-behalf email change end to end in a single synchronous mutation without any direct database edits, and the action is fully reflected in the audit trail with outcome = `committed`.
+- **SC-002**: Across all completed email changes, zero observed cases of divergence between the Alkemio user record and the identity provider identity (i.e., zero cases where one side reflects the new email and the other does not), excluding cases explicitly recorded as `drift_detected` (which are the result of rollback-budget exhaustion and require admin reconciliation per FR-009b).
+- **SC-003**: For every email change attempt — successful, rolled-back, drift-detected, drift-resolved, drift-resolution-failed, validation-rejected, conflict-rejected — the platform produces an audit entry within the same operation; spot-checking 100% of attempts in a test run yields an audit entry for each.
+- **SC-004**: Failed second-side commits in a fault-injection test produce zero residual changes on either side and surface a clear, distinct error to the admin.
+- **SC-005**: A double-failure (forward Kratos write fails AND the Kratos revert fails) produces a `drift_detected` audit entry capturing the observed value on each side, a Winston error log entry tagged `email_change_drift_detected`, and an Elastic APM `captureError` invocation with the same marker.
+- **SC-006**: Validation errors (format, uniqueness, no-change) are returned without invoking any side-write; the audit entry records the rejection outcome and the database state is unchanged.

comments.body: Skipping — this is a deliberate, reconciled spec decision, not a residual conflict. The spec no longer carries a blanket "no email in audit" rule: FR-014 only forbids leaking *conflicting-account existence* in `failure_reason` fields. Storing the audited `oldEmail`/`newEmail` in `platform_audit_entry.details` (JSONB) is intentional and forensically required (FR-014a). FR-014b draws the distinction explicitly: the audited old/new addresses ARE exposed, while the initiator/subject *current* email is not (only `{id, displayName}`). The original finding referenced the earlier `email_change_audit_entry` design with typed `old_email`/`new_email` columns; that design has since been generalised, but emails are still deliberately retained.
